messages.text: Quick q on personal trading pre-clearance: someone in Wealth asked if a spouse's brokerage account needs pre-clear when the spouse trades independently. Policy section 4 reads ambiguous to me. Anyone know the answer?

Short answer: yes if it's a household member and the employee has any influence or benefit from the account. The covered-persons definition includes immediate family sharing a household. Check the Code of Ethics appendix B.
Got it, that matches how I read appendix B. I'll tell them to submit through the pre-clear form and attach the spouse's broker statement.

FYI for the pre-clear tool: we're adding a restricted list check against the live Project-side watch list before approval goes out. Today it only checks at submit time, so approvals can go stale. Planning to ship next sprint.

Good. We had a case last quarter where approval was granted at 9:40 and the name hit the restricted list at 11:00. Trade went at 10:15 so it was fine, but it was close. What's the approval validity window now?
Currently end of business day, same day only. I'd propose we keep that but re-validate at trade-time via the broker feed, and flag if the list changed since approval.

Separate thing: reviewing onboarding for {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0130}} and noticed the client's brokerage account {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00275}} is linked to an employee referral. Does that trigger any personal-trading disclosure on our side, or only if the employee holds an interest?

Only if the employee has a beneficial interest or discretion over it. A plain referral isn't a covered account. If James Anderson manages it as RM, that's normal coverage, no pre-clear. Just confirm no family tie.
Makes sense. I'll note in the file that no beneficial interest was found and move on. Thanks.

Reminder: pre-clear form now has a required field for holding period acknowledgement (30 days). Old submissions without it will bounce back from tomorrow. Ping me if anyone sees odd validation errors.
Will do. I'll mention it in the compliance huddle Wednesday so nobody gets surprised.
